tools.name: list_companies
tools.description:
List companies accessible to the current user. Returns [{title, slug, role}].
Use slug (not title) in all other tools.

Args:
    search: Case-insensitive filter on title or slug.

tools.name: list_programs
tools.description:
List program slugs for a company.

Args:
    company: Company slug (from list_companies)

tools.name: get_program_info
tools.description:
Fetch program rules, scopes, rewards, poc_required, focus_area, and dual_defence flag.
Check this before triaging to verify scope and severity/reward expectations.

Args:
    program: Program slug (e.g. mawari-sc-audit)

tools.name: get_hacker_info
tools.description:
Fetch a hacker's profile: rank, reputation, reports count, verified/kyc
status, country, skills, influenced programs, social links, and payout stats
(severity counts + total_bounty — may be hidden when display_payout_stats=False).

Args:
    nickname: Hacker nickname (e.g. 'sensei')

tools.name: get_program_stats
tools.description:
Report counts: total, new, SLA soon-to-breach, SLA breached.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    program: Program slug

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description:
Search/filter reports. Returns summaries (id, title, state, severity, labels, author, created).
Use get_report_details for full content. page=0 fetches all pages (slow for large programs).

Args:
    company: Company slug
    program: Program slug
    search: Free-text search query
    severity: "Critical" | "High" | "Medium" | "Low"
    state: "New" | "In review" | "Need more info" | "Triaged" | "Out of scope" | "Not applicable" | "Spam" | "Informative" | "Disclosed" | "Duplicate" | "Resolved" | "Paid"
    labels: Filter by label names (OR filter — reports matching any of the provided labels are returned)
    hide_closed: Show only open reports (New, In review, Need more info, Triaged, Paid)
    page: 1-based page number (10/page). 0 = all pages.
    created_after: Return reports created on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
    created_before: Return reports created on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Use same value as created_after to filter a single day.
    awaiting_reply: Return only reports whose most recent comment is from the reporter, i.e. the ones waiting on a response from your team. Use it to build a "needs reply" queue. Leave False to apply no filter; the opposite set (reports your team answered last) cannot be requested.

tools.name: get_report_sizes
tools.description:
Get char counts for each report field without fetching full content.
Call this first to decide whether to fetch the full report or specific fields.

Returns: {vulnerability_description, validation_steps, comments, attachments}

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)

tools.name: get_report_details
tools.description:
Fetch report content. Default truncates long fields at 4000 chars and excludes comments;
_sizes shows real char counts. Use get_report_sizes first to plan what to fetch.

- full=True: return everything at full length including comments (may be large)
- fields=["vulnerability_description"]: return only that field at full length
- fields=["comments"]: get comments inline

Available fields: id, title, severity, state, author, target, attachments,
                  vulnerability_description, validation_steps, comments,
                  labels, created_at, published_at, updated_at, sla, cvss_score

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    fields: Return only these fields at full length.
    full: Return all fields at full length including comments.

tools.name: get_reports_details_batch
tools.description:
Fetch details for multiple reports. Same truncation/fields logic as get_report_details.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_ids: Report IDs to fetch
    fields: Return only these fields at full length (omit for default truncated response).

tools.name: get_comments
tools.description:
Get comments on a report. Deleted comments are always excluded.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    limit: Return only the last N comments (most recent first).
    include_hidden: If False, exclude comments hidden from the reporter.
    comment_ids: Return only comments with these IDs (from list_comments_summary).

tools.name: list_comments_summary
tools.description:
List comment metadata without fetching comment text. Use this to identify
which comments to fetch with get_comments(comment_ids=[...]).

Returns: [{comment_id, username, role, date, is_hidden}] excluding deleted comments.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)

tools.name: search_comments
tools.description:
Search comment text across all reports in a program. Slow on large programs — use page=N to limit scope.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    program: Program slug
    query: Text to find (case-insensitive)
    state: Restrict to reports in these states
    page: 1-based page of reports to search. 0 = all pages.

tools.name: get_attachments
tools.description:
List attachment filenames and URLs for a report.
Only includes report-level attachments (description/PoC uploads). Comment attachments
are not listed here — check the attachments field in get_comments results instead.
URLs require auth — use fetch_attachment to read content into context, or
download_attachment to save a file locally.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)

tools.name: fetch_attachment
tools.description:
Download an attachment via authenticated session. Text files return up to
4000 characters of content per call, plus a short marker when more remains —
when truncated is true, call again with the offset from that marker. Binary
files return metadata only; their bytes are never returned — call
download_attachment to save them locally.
Every call re-downloads and re-decodes the whole file — there is no server-side
cache to page through — so continuing a large file repeatedly is expensive.
Jump to a specific offset deliberately rather than paging through start to
finish.
To attach a file to a comment, pass its URL as attachment_url to
comment_with_attachment instead of downloading it.

Args:
    attachment_url: URL from get_attachments or get_report_details
    offset: Character offset into the text content. Use to continue a truncated read.

tools.name: list_labels
tools.description:
List all labels available in the company. Labels are company-level and shared across all programs.
Use this before triaging to pick correct existing labels instead of creating duplicates.

Args:
    company: Company slug

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description:
Post a markdown comment on a report. Visible to the researcher unless hidden=True.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    comment: Markdown text. Newlines are supported.
    hidden: If true, only triage team can see the comment.

tools.name: comment_with_attachment
tools.description:
Post a comment with one or more file attachments on a report.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    attachments: List of attachment dicts. Each dict:
        {"attachment_url": "https://dashboard.hackenproof.com/attachments/..."}
        to copy an existing HackenProof attachment, or {"file_path": "/abs/path"}
        for a local file. attachment_url is fetched server-side. file_path works
        only over stdio. Optional "filename" overrides the stored name.
    comment: Markdown comment text. Newlines are supported.
    hidden: If true, only triage team can see the comment.

tools.name: screenshot_and_comment
tools.description:
Attach an evidence rendering of another HackenProof report (e.g. the
original of a duplicate) to a comment.

Behaviour: fetches the report's PDF first (full content, fast). Falls back
to a page screenshot only if the PDF endpoint fails for that report.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID to post the comment on (e.g. HACK-55)
    screenshot_url: Full URL of the report page to attach (e.g. the original duplicate).
    comment: Markdown comment text. Newlines are supported.
    hidden: If true, only triage team can see the comment.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.description:
Edit a comment on a report, possible only within 15 minutes of posting.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    new_text: Replacement markdown text.
    comment_id: ID of the comment to edit (preferred if available).
    comment_text: Substring of the comment text to search for (used when comment_id is unknown).

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description:
Delete a comment on a report, possible only within 15 minutes of posting.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    comment_id: ID of the comment to delete (preferred if available).
    comment_text: Substring of the comment text to search for (used when comment_id is unknown).

tools.name: change_state
tools.description:
Change report state. Automatically walks intermediate transitions to reach the target.

Valid target states: New | In review | Need more info | Triaged | Out of scope |
                     Not applicable | Spam | Informative | Disclosed | Duplicate | Resolved
Transition to Paid is rejected — payout is a separate operation.

When target_state="Disclosed", you can optionally control public visibility:
- visibility: "private" | "partially" | "public"
- visibility_params: per-field booleans. Recognised keys:
    report_title, author_name, rewards, comments, target_info, vuln_details,
    validation_steps, vuln_type, attachments, severity, state, creation_date,
    participants, timeline
These are ignored unless target_state="Disclosed". Use the set_visibility tool to
update them later on an already-disclosed report.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    target_state: Target state (exact string from list above)
    visibility: Public-visibility mode for disclosed reports
    visibility_params: Per-field visibility toggles for disclosed reports

tools.name: set_visibility
tools.description:
Update what's publicly visible on an already-disclosed report.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    visibility: "private" | "partially" | "public"
    visibility_params: Per-field booleans. Recognised keys:
        report_title, author_name, rewards, comments, target_info, vuln_details,
        validation_steps, vuln_type, attachments, severity, state, creation_date,
        participants, timeline

tools.name: change_severity
tools.description:
Change report severity.

Valid values: Low | Medium | High | Critical

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    severity: New severity (exact string from list above)

tools.name: add_labels
tools.description:
Add labels to a report.
Use kebab-case: dup-42, access-control, needs-poc. Avoid spaces/underscores/mixed case.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    labels: Label names to add

tools.name: remove_labels
tools.description:
Remove labels from a report. Labels not currently on the report are silently ignored.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    labels: Label names to remove

tools.name: triage_report
tools.description:
Apply all triage decisions to a single report in one authorized action.

For the same actions on many reports, use triage_bulk instead.
For different actions per report, use triage_reports_batch.

Execution order: comment (with optional attachments) → state → severity → labels.
The LLM should present a plain-text summary of planned actions before calling this,
so the user can review and confirm in one step.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_id: Report ID (e.g. HACK-55)
    state: Target state (e.g. "Out of scope", "Duplicate", "Triaged")
    severity: New severity (e.g. "High", "Critical")
    labels_add: Labels to add (e.g. ["dup-42", "needs-poc"])
    labels_remove: Labels to remove (e.g. ["needs-poc"])
    comment: Markdown comment text
    comment_hidden: If true, comment is only visible to triage team
    screenshot_url: If set, takes an authenticated screenshot and attaches it to the comment
    attachments: Files to attach. Each dict:
        {"attachment_url": "https://dashboard.hackenproof.com/attachments/..."}
        or {"file_path": "/abs/path"} (stdio only). Optional "filename"
        overrides the stored name.

tools.name: triage_reports_batch
tools.description:
Apply different triage decisions to multiple reports in one authorized action.

For the same actions on all reports, use triage_bulk instead (simpler, flat params).

The LLM should present a summary table of planned actions before calling this,
so the user can review, edit, and confirm everything in one step.

Each entry in `reports` is a dict with (all fields optional except report_id):
    report_id       (str, required)
    state           (str)  e.g. "Out of scope", "Duplicate", "Triaged"
    severity        (str)  e.g. "High", "Critical"
    labels_add      (list[str])
    labels_remove   (list[str])
    comment         (str)  markdown text
    comment_hidden  (bool) default false
    screenshot_url  (str)  if set, attaches a screenshot to the comment
    attachments     (list[dict]) file attachments:
                    {"attachment_url": "..."} | {"file_path": "..."}
                    optional "filename" overrides the stored name

Execution order per report: comment (+attachments) → state → severity → labels.
Reports are processed sequentially; failures on one report do not stop the rest.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    reports: List of per-report action dicts

tools.name: triage_bulk
tools.description:
Apply identical triage actions to multiple reports at once.

Use this when the same state, severity, labels, and/or comment apply to all reports.
For per-report customization, use triage_reports_batch instead.

Execution order per report: comment (+attachments) → state → severity → labels.
Reports are processed sequentially; failures on one do not stop the rest.

Args:
    company: Company slug
    report_ids: List of report IDs (e.g. ["HACK-55", "HACK-56"])
    state: Target state (e.g. "Out of scope", "Duplicate")
    severity: New severity (e.g. "High", "Critical")
    labels_add: Labels to add
    labels_remove: Labels to remove
    comment: Markdown comment text
    comment_hidden: If true, comment is only visible to triage team
    screenshot_url: Takes an authenticated screenshot and attaches it to each comment
    attachments: Files to attach. Each dict:
        {"attachment_url": "https://dashboard.hackenproof.com/attachments/..."}
        or {"file_path": "/abs/path"} (stdio only). Optional "filename"
        overrides the stored name.
